**Finding submitted — ASSIGN: deviation (preferred-level cure proposed).**

**What I found across the responsive locations**

- **§10.2(a) (p0406)** — the operative assignment clause. Consent is owed to the Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee, Certificateholders and 66-2/3% Controlling Class Noteholders — *not* to us (Issuer/Depositor) — and there is no "not unreasonably withheld" standard. It also carves out §7.6 in full.
- **§7.6 (p0348)** — clause (d) lets Cellco assign the Agreement to any Affiliate of the Servicer with no consent from us. That is the substantive gap: a standing no-consent assignment route for the counterparty.
- **§5.3 (p0249)** — our side is already covered: merger, consolidation, succession to the Depositor's business, and assignment to a Depositor Affiliate all pass by right (preferred elements 1 and 2 already met).
- **§7.1 (p0314)** — the Servicer may resign only if legally unable to perform; there is no change-of-control exit against us (preferred element 6 already met). §7.2 termination events run in our favour and were not flagged.

**Why preferred rather than fallback:** reaching the fallback would have required stripping the no-consent affiliate route from *both* §5.3 and §7.6, downgrading our own assignment freedom and forcing collateral rewrites of the "or assignment" references throughout those sections. The preferred target keeps §5.3 verbatim and tightens only the Servicer.

**The change (two operations, validated ok:true):** narrow the §7.6 carve-out to exclude clause (d), add the Issuer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld), and add a one-sentence competitor bar. Every untouched word of §10.2(a) is preserved.
